claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?** If yes, how many children and what are their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child - Alex, who's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 18 years old, I need to ask some important questions about their current situation.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, studying at school, college, or university, or in approved training programs)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - doing A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and in approved education, I need to understand a bit more about their circumstances.

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't work that much - no full-time job or anything like that. As for benefits, I'm not sure whether Alex receives anything in their own right. I don't think so, but I'm honestly not certain about that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To be clear, you don't believe Alex is receiving benefits in their own right, but you're not completely certain - is that correct?

**Also, could you confirm whether you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, that's right - I don't think Alex is getting any benefits, but I'm not 100% certain.

And yes, I do live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you currently responsible for Alex - meaning you either live with Alex (which you've mentioned you do) or you're paying toward their upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely - Alex lives at home with me, so I'm definitely responsible for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another relative)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

**Here's the situation:**

You meet most of the key eligibility requirements:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is 18 and in approved education (A-levels), which falls within the eligible age range (under 20 and in approved education or training)
- You're responsible for Alex, who lives with you
- Alex doesn't work 24 hours or more per week
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**However,** there's one critical piece of information we need to confirm: whether Alex is receiving any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit, Employment and Support Allowance, or similar benefits). If Alex does receive such benefits, you would **not** be eligible for Child Benefit.

**What you should do:**
I recommend checking with Alex or reviewing any correspondence from the Department for Work and Pensions to confirm whether Alex is claiming any benefits independently. Once you have this information, you'll know for certain whether you're eligible to claim Child Benefit.

If Alex is **not** receiving benefits in their own right, then you would be eligible to claim Child Benefit.
